Kit

kit/ui — stock-theme widgets

6 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Widget creation, refresh, and ownershipAPI by taskAdopting your own scenesWorked example (cavecrawl)Layout and lifecycle constraintsNetgraph

kit/ui builds a lobby, chat box, scoreboard, interaction prompt, inventory and hotbar, hp bar, and abilities bar from Godot controls. It uses the stock Godot theme and requires no scene assets. Theme the returned nodes or supply custom scenes through scene adoption.

Widgets read session state such as roster, stats, and chat, plus values the game supplies. They work with either replication lane; the netgraph displays both coop and simulation statistics. HUD examples use coop fields such as kit/combat cooldowns. A simulation game passes its corresponding fields to the same widgets.

Odin
import kui "godot:kit/ui"

Widget creation, refresh, and ownership#

Call *_make with a parent node to build controls and receive their handles. The game connects buttons and input, then calls *_refresh when displayed state changes. Lobby, chat, and scoreboard refresh on events; the local HUD refreshes during frames to show live values. *_destroy releases tracking arrays only. The scene owns the nodes and frees them with their parent.

Refresh procedures reuse row Labels and hide unused rows rather than rebuilding them on each update.

The public API accepts string, so callers can pass fmt.tprintf results without converting to cstring. Widget implementations perform the engine string conversion.

API by task#

Lobby provides a title, status line, live roster, and three buttons:

Odin
lobby_make :: proc(parent: gd.Node, title: string) -> Lobby
lobby_destroy :: proc(l: ^Lobby)
lobby_set_status :: proc(l: ^Lobby, text: string)
lobby_show_menu :: proc(l: ^Lobby, menu: bool, start: bool)
lobby_show_code :: proc(l: ^Lobby, show: bool)   // reveal the join-code field
lobby_code :: proc(l: ^Lobby) -> string          // entered code, trimmed and uppercased; temporary allocation
lobby_refresh :: proc(l: ^Lobby, s: ^ksess.Session)

Connect handlers to Lobby's host_btn, join_btn, and start_btn, each a gd.Button. start_btn is initially hidden; the game shows it through lobby_show_menu when its start conditions are met.

lobby_refresh reads the session roster in stable Player_Id join order. It marks the host with a crown, the local player with (you), and departed players with dimmed (away) text. Measured ping comes from the session stat registry. Relay games call lobby_show_code in ready() to reveal the code field above Join. The Join handler reads lobby_code; "" selects address-based joining.

Chat box provides a bounded scrollback of kit/comms lines plus a Line_Edit (CHAT_SHOW :: 8 rows painted; the comms log keeps more):

Odin
chat_make :: proc(parent: gd.Node) -> Chat
chat_destroy :: proc(ch: ^Chat)
chat_show :: proc(ch: ^Chat, visible: bool)
chat_clear_input :: proc(ch: ^Chat)
chat_refresh :: proc(ch: ^Chat, c: ^kcomms.Comms)
chat_submit :: proc(ch: ^Chat, c: ^kcomms.Comms, text: gd.String, sent: ^bool = nil)

Chat displays speech as name: text and system lines as * text. Connect chat.input's text_submitted signal to a handler that calls chat_submit. It extracts and clamps the text, sends it, clears the input, and releases focus so movement keys such as WASD return to gameplay. The optional sent latch prevents the submitting Enter key from immediately reopening chat when Enter is also bound to "talk".

Scoreboard displays the session stat columns the game registered, including measured ping, damage/kills/deaths recorded through kit/combat, and game-specific counters. kit/ui reads those columns without declaring them:

Odin
score_make :: proc(parent: gd.Node) -> Score
score_destroy :: proc(sb: ^Score)
score_show :: proc(sb: ^Score, visible: bool)          // show while Tab is held
score_hide :: proc(sb: ^Score, name: string)           // hide a column by name
score_refresh :: proc(sb: ^Score, s: ^ksess.Session)

Departed players remain listed with their accumulated stats. Some registered columns carry game state that should stay off the scoreboard, such as Scrapyard's look/iron loadout choices or the muster's ready bit. Call score_hide once after declaring those columns. Unknown names are ignored.

HUD provides a prompt, inventory/hotbar, hp, and abilities:

Odin
prompt_make :: proc(parent: gd.Node) -> Prompt
prompt_set :: proc(p: ^Prompt, text: string)           // "" hides the prompt

inv_make :: proc(parent: gd.Node, capacity: int) -> Inv
inv_show :: proc(inv: ^Inv, visible: bool)
inv_refresh :: proc(inv: ^Inv, slots: []kitems.Slot, table: ^kitems.Table, selected := -1)
inv_destroy :: proc(inv: ^Inv)

hp_make :: proc(parent: gd.Node) -> Hp_Bar
hp_refresh :: proc(hb: ^Hp_Bar, current, max_hp: i32)

abilities_make :: proc(parent: gd.Node, capacity: int) -> Abilities_Bar
abilities_refresh :: proc(bar: ^Abilities_Bar, defs: []kcombat.Ability_Def, cds: []u16, resource: i32, tick_hz: int)
abilities_destroy :: proc(bar: ^Abilities_Bar)

HUD widgets render text using the stock theme. The hp bar displays hp ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░ 70/100, which a test can read from the node tree. Abilities display [rock] when ready, [rock 1.2s] while cooling down, or [rock $] when ready but unaffordable.

Cooldown values count ticks, so pass the rate of the loop that decrements them as tick_hz. Use session_tick_hz(&ses) for coop cooldowns or the simulation lane's rate for simulated cooldowns. This converts the displayed duration to seconds at the configured rate.

Both ability storage models use kcombat.Ability_Def rows. A slot-array game passes its Cooldowns array as c.cds[:]; a play-block game gathers its countdowns beside the same definitions, such as []u16{r.slime.cd, r.ignite.cd}. Pass selected to display the inventory row as a hotbar.

Adopting your own scenes#

To use an authored lobby, chat, or scoreboard, build its scene in the editor and pass it through Boot's Options.lobby_scene / chat_scene / score_scene; see boot.md. Kit instantiates the scene and finds its required controls by name at any depth. Those controls receive the standard behavior, while the game controls additional nodes and appearance. A missing required node produces a log message once during boot and leaves the widget inactive without crashing.

Odin
lobby_adopt :: proc(parent: gd.Node, scene: gd.Packed_Scene, title: string) -> Lobby
chat_adopt :: proc(parent: gd.Node, scene: gd.Packed_Scene) -> Chat
score_adopt :: proc(parent: gd.Node, scene: gd.Packed_Scene) -> Score

Each widget requires these node names:

  • Lobby: Title (Label), Status (Label), Players (a container for roster rows), Host (Button), Join (Button), and Start (Button, initially hidden). Join-code games can add an optional Code (LineEdit) revealed by lobby_show_code; omitting it is supported.
  • Chat: Lines (a container for scrollback rows) and Input (LineEdit).
  • Scoreboard: Grid (GridContainer). Kit sets its column count and adds the cells.

Authored scenes control their layout. Anchors under Boot's layer bind to the viewport; stock sizing and scoreboard centering are skipped. Kit creates row and cell Labels, which inherit themes from the scene root. After boot_attach, use the widget's root to connect extra controls such as a Single Player button or address field.

Worked example (cavecrawl)#

Odin
self.ui = kui.lobby_make(self.owner, "C A V E C R A W L")
kui.lobby_set_status(&self.ui, "Host a cave, or join one at localhost")
gd.connect_to(cast(gd.Object)self.ui.host_btn, "pressed", self.owner, "on_host")
gd.connect_to(cast(gd.Object)self.ui.join_btn, "pressed", self.owner, "on_join")
gd.connect_to(cast(gd.Object)self.ui.start_btn, "pressed", self.owner, "on_start")

self.chat = kui.chat_make(self.owner)
kui.chat_show(&self.chat, false)   // hide chat before connecting its input handler
gd.connect_to(cast(gd.Object)self.chat.input, "text_submitted", self.owner, "on_chat")

// Position the status controls at the top-left.
// Widget creation places them at the anchor origin by default.
gd.control_set_position(cast(gd.Control)self.hud_hp.label, {8, 4}, false)
gd.control_set_position(self.hud_ab.root, {8, 22}, false)
gd.control_set_position(self.inv.root, {8, 40}, false)

Refresh the local player's HUD during frame processing. Host mutations do not produce received-state events, so an event-only refresh would miss them:

Odin
kui.hp_refresh(&self.hud_hp, hp_view(self.me_spel), MAX_HP)
defs := [?]kcombat.Ability_Def{ROCK_ABILITY, HEAL_ABILITY}
kui.abilities_refresh(&self.hud_ab, defs[:], self.me_spel.cds[:], self.me_spel.stamina, ksess.session_tick_hz(&self.ses))

Layout and lifecycle constraints#

  • Set grow directions alongside anchors. An auto-sizing label at the bottom edge can grow downward off-screen. Pair control_set_anchors_preset with grow directions and anchor-relative offsets, as the prompt does:

    Odin
    gd.control_set_anchors_preset(cast(gd.Control)p.label, .Preset_Center_Bottom, false)
gd.control_set_v_grow_direction(cast(gd.Control)p.label, .Grow_Direction_Begin)  // grow upward
gd.control_set_h_grow_direction(cast(gd.Control)p.label, .Grow_Direction_Both)   // keep centered
gd.control_set_offset(cast(gd.Control)p.label, .Top, -34)                        // lifted baseline,
gd.control_set_offset(cast(gd.Control)p.label, .Bottom, -34)                     // tracks resizes

  • Look up the host id. lobby_refresh crowns session_host(s). A resumed host keeps its old id (see save.md), so do not hardcode player id 1 as the host.

  • Refresh lists on events. Call lobby_refresh on session events, chat_refresh on Ev_Line, and score_refresh on Ev_Stats_Updated. Refresh the local HUD each frame for live cooldowns and host-written state.

  • Release tracking arrays separately from nodes. *_destroy frees the Odin arrays used by lobby/chat/score/inv/abilities to reuse rows stored in a [dynamic]. The scene owns their nodes. kboot.boot_detach destroys those arrays before queuing their container subtree for deletion. Freeing only the game node releases the nodes but leaks tracking arrays until process exit. Call boot_detach while the game process remains alive.

  • prompt/hp need no *_destroy. Each holds only a Label node freed with its parent. A netgraph holds a Label and a fixed sparkline array; netgraph_destroy zeroes it for consistent teardown calls. The game owns its custom netgraph, while Boot supplies its data through boot_net_stats.

  • Position widgets after creation; their initial position is the anchor origin.

Netgraph#

Create a network overlay with netgraph_make, control its visibility with netgraph_show, and update it with netgraph_refresh(ng, Net_Stats{...}):

Code
net  42ms  jit 6ms  loss 1.2%  ok
rate rx 120p/s 3.2k/s · tx 48p/s 0.4k/s
rx 3.2k state 2.1 stream 0.8 app16 0.2 · tx 0.4k cmd 0.3
sim  lead 4t  resim ▁▁▂▁▇▁▁…  rec 128  gap 2  ack 3t  rw 12t  cpu 0.42ms  cq 0
snap full 2% delta 98% rows 428 quiet 2100 defer 3 aoi 900 18.2k
warn  rclamp 3▲

The first row shows RTT from the replicated ping stat (net_ping_ms) plus jitter and loss from ENet's per-peer statistics. Clients obtain the host connection's values through netgd.wire_link_quality. The quality label prioritizes loss, then jitter, then RTT. The rate row reports the last completed one-second packet and byte window.

The traffic row groups bytes by message kind. Supply Net_Stats.traffic = netgd.wire_traffic(&boot.wire) as an opaque value so kit/ui remains independent of the transport package. The simulation row shows input lead and gaps, age of the last fully applied snapshot acknowledgement, the authority's rewind envelope, replay cost since refresh, and command queue pressure. The snapshot row shows full/delta proportions, unchanged-row suppression, budget deferrals, AOI culling, and bytes.

The resimulation sparkline shows bursts of client replay work. A flat baseline means no recent replay; lost inputs and contested prediction errors can produce spikes even when correction smoothing hides their visible effect. Every field is optional; coop games leave sim false. Use kboot.boot_net_stats(&boot) for Boot's coop statistics and the simulation projection when boot_lane is installed.

The warn row appears when diagnostic counters are nonzero. It includes guard_hits for client writes to authority-owned fields, input_drops for dropped simulation inputs, cmd_capped for commands refused by the per-player cap, and rewind_clamped for queries limited by measured-link bounds, render-hint limits, or the absolute rewind configuration.

boot_net_stats fills malformed-message, access/predicate, traffic-budget, and write-guard counters for every game. An installed lane adds simulation counters. The overlay prints each nonzero count and marks increases since the previous refresh with ▲. A single clamp before timing settles can be normal; a count still rising a minute into play needs investigation. The change marker distinguishes current failures from accumulated startup counts.
